collection.credit:
NEW EVENTS — FEARS AND DOUBTS (FEA-01..50, draft for the owner, 2026-11-15)
Fears big and small, sensible and not, self-doubt, feeling like a fraud, dread with no reason, wanting and fearing the same thing, and courage that is still frightened. Nobody has to be brave, nobody is mocked, and a fear does not have to be conquered by the end.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. Edit anything and send it back; nothing ships until you approve.

ledger.why: the casting line, carried out as the roles' ages (picks two teens aged 14-17)

collection.description: A fast teen fears that winning the swimming race means always having to win: swim flat out, or hold back a little.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: (subject) has entered the swimming race for the first time, and (subject.he/she) is fast. Very fast. Fast enough that (subject.he/she) might win. And that's the problem: if (subject.he/she) wins, people will expect (subject.him/her) to win every year. (subject.He/she) is standing at the water's edge, wondering whether to swim properly. (friend) is beside (subject.him/her), stretching.

choices.label: Swim as Fast as You Can

o1.name: Outcome A
o1.text: (subject) swims as fast as (subject.he/she) can, and wins, by a long way. Everyone cheers. Within an hour someone says, "See you win again next year!" and (subject)'s stomach drops. (subject.He/she) was right to worry about that. (subject.He/she) also won. Both things are true, and (subject.he/she) isn't sure how to feel.

o2.name: Outcome B
o2.text: (subject) swims well but not as fast as (subject.he/she) could, and comes third. Nobody expects anything. (subject.He/she) feels relieved, and then, later, a little cross with (subject.him/her)self. (subject.He/she) doesn't know which feeling is the right one. Maybe next year (subject.he/she) will find out what would have happened. Maybe not.
